simple.meaning: סְבָלָה (çᵉbâlâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “porterage.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: סְבָלָה (H5450) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 1:11, with occurrences in Exodus.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סְבָלָה (H5450) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in סְבָלָה (H5450) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: סְבָלָה (çᵉbâlâh) / H5450 is traced through Exodus 1:11, Exodus 2:11, Exodus 5:4, Exodus 5:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

timeline.evidenceText: Therefore they set taskmasters over them to afflict them with their burdens. They built storage cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Raamses.
In those days, when Moses had grown up, he went out to his brothers and saw their burdens. He saw an Egyptian striking a Hebrew, one of his brothers.
The king of Egypt said to them, “Why do you, Moses and Aaron, take the people from their work? Get back to your burdens!”
Pharaoh said, “Behold, the people of the land are now many, and you make them rest from their burdens.”

Therefore tell the children of Israel, ‘I am Yahweh, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments.
I will take you to myself for a people. I will be your God; and you shall know that I am Yahweh your God, who brings you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.

definitions.full: H5450. siblah [ סִבְלָה ] noun feminine burden ; — plural construct מִצְרַיִם סִבְלֹת Exod 6:6 (P), of the heavy labours imposed on Israel by Egyptian, 6:7 ; suffix סִבְלֹתֵיכֶם 5:4 (J), סִבְלֹתָם 1:11 ; 5:5 (both J), 2:11 (E); (compare Psa 81:7 , סֵבֶל ).
